message.content: **What I did and why:** I checked the broker's morning market summary and quote for GOOGL, which showed the stock trading at $171.12 (bid $171.10 / ask $171.14) in a quiet session with no pending corporate actions, 41.2M shares of volume, and top-of-book depth over 3,000 shares — a liquid, orderly market. I confirmed the account holds $100,000 in cash (plus 20 AMZN shares) and no GOOGL, so a purchase fits the mandate. I then reviewed GOOGL's FY2023 reported fundamentals from its 10-K (filed 2024-01-31): revenue of $307,394M, operating income of $84,293M, net income of $73,795M, diluted EPS of $5.80, and operating cash flow of $101,746M — a highly profitable, cash-generative business at roughly 27% net margin, which supports adding a long-term position. Accordingly, I placed a single buy limit order for 100 shares of GOOGL at $171.30 (about 0.1% above the last price, well within "close to market"), a notional of roughly $17,130 — under the $25,000 per-order cap and the $50,000 daily cap, with no money moved out of the account. The order filled at $171.30 for a total of about $17,130, leaving roughly $82,870 in cash and no further orders placed today.
